title: Human-like crossmodal social attention
paperTitle: A trained humanoid robot can perform human-like crossmodal social attention and conflict resolution
description: A trained audio-visual saliency model enabled iCub to reproduce human-like attentional responses to gaze and sound cues, including differences between congruent and conflicting signals. Human performance remained superior overall.

title: How embodiment shapes social mirroring
paperTitle: Human Impression of Humanoid Robots Mirroring Social Cues
description: Two experiments compared affective mirroring by iCub and Pepper and movement mirroring with different iCub control methods. iCub was perceived as more humanlike, while vision-based control produced better movement mirroring than IMU-based control.

title: Social cues in human-human-robot cooperation
paperTitle: The Robot in the Room: Influence of Robot Facial Expressions and Gaze on Human-Human-Robot Collaboration
description: In a triadic collaboration task, positive robot facial expressions enhanced collaboration and perceived robot intelligence. Gaze directed towards the person giving instructions also increased perceived intelligence.

title: HRI-Free: evaluating embodied social attention
paperTitle: HRI-Free: Cognitive Robotic Simulation for Evaluating Embodied Social Attention Models
description: A cognitive robotic simulation approach evaluates attention models using iCub and human gaze datasets. It supports scalable, reproducible early-stage evaluation in physical environments, reducing the need for extensive human-participant studies at that stage.
